ToyIndex: Reusing Document Layout for Fast Retrieval (synthetic fixture)
Ana Example [1]; Boreal Group [2]
[1] Acorn Institute. [2] Boreal Lab.
Preprint posted: 2026-01.
Abstract: Repeated document search wastes time encoding unchanged layouts. ToyIndex caches layout features and updates only edited regions to reduce query latency while preserving retrieval quality.

Document retrieval repeatedly encodes unchanged layouts. LiteScan [1] reduces image resolution, but loses small-text details. Our question is whether reusing layout features can reduce repeated-search latency without reducing retrieval quality.

ToyIndex builds a page-layout cache once. When a document changes, a region hash selects changed regions for re-encoding; the retriever combines refreshed regions with cached features. On synthetic MiniDocs v1 test, using one ExampleGPU, batch size 1 and FP16, ToyIndex reaches Recall@10 92.0% with query latency 12 ms; LiteScan reaches Recall@10 89.0% with query latency 20 ms. Latency excludes initial cache construction.

The cache assumes stable layout coordinates; large page rearrangements require rebuilding it. Monetary cost is not reported. References: [1] Ivo Sample et al. LiteScan: Low-Resolution Document Retrieval. 2024.
